comment: splanc HITL fleet catalog (fleet-identical; baked into every rig image, read by hitl-reserved --catalog). USB ESP32-C6 boards are auto-discovered; network DUTs (a Pi player) are runtime-seeded via scripts/seed-network-dut.sh into the seeded_file below (no redeploy). The FX2 logic analyzer is a shared resource, dormant unless an FX2 is attached. Per-rig values (the provisioning-AP SSID/PSK = hostname) are passed as flags by nix/hitl-app.nix, not baked here. Ports 2222-2233 match the firewall range opened in hitl-app.nix.

shared_resources.comment: One FX2/fx2lafw logic analyzer whose channels tap each unit's LED line. Dormant unless an FX2 is physically attached (the broker self-gates via FX2Present). The default map taps D0/ws2812 so a discovered single-board rig captures its sole unit; per-unit channels are set at runtime via `hitl shared logic-analyzer '{"op":"map.set",...}'` (persisted under /var/lib/hitl).
shared_resources.name: logic-analyzer

discovery.comment: Auto-discover attached ESP32-C6 player boards by their built-in USB-JTAG by-id symlinks (one reservable unit per board, sticky ports, live hot-plug), and ingest runtime-seeded units (a network DUT Pi) from seeded_file. USB ports 2222-2229; seeded ports 2230-2233 (dedicated range above the USB pool). Each discovered unit unions in the analyzer tap cap from the broker's channel map. chip_overrides pins boards a bare USB scan can't disambiguate: the ESP32-C3 and ESP32-C6 share the native USB-JTAG PID (303a:1001), so a C3 would default to esp32c6/c6-; each override keys a board's MAC (its USB serial, matched case-/separator-insensitively) to the right type + name_prefix. rig-3's third DUT (/dev/ttyACM2, MAC AC:27:6E:7F:18:60) is an ESP32-C3.
